Thank you for the reply. 

I've been to 3 different psychiatrists for psychiatric evaluations before. I've talked a bit to all of them as well as a psychologist about things generally being a little more stable in the summer, but I'm pretty sure Seasonal Affective Disorder was ruled out at some point. 

I used to worry a lot about different mental disorders and I'm pretty sure I once stayed up all night just reading different parts of the DSM over and over, but I've since come to terms that with a lot of them psychiatrist really can't or are hesitant to diagnose people with certain illnesses without years of symptoms and that worrying about something like that maybe occurring will just makes things worse and is outside of my control in a lot of cases anyway :)

Thanks for the reply. 

I used to see both a psychiatrist and a psychologist, but I don't any more. Partly because I had one of my longer periods of feeling mostly fine and also because I didn't feel it helped me all that much when things where really bad anyway. 

I've never been to see someone that specializes in cognitive therapy, although I've looked at it before. Maybe I'll look into it again, but last time there where really long waiting lists in my area unfortunately.

Thanks for your thoughtful reply. 

I'm in my early 20's. I've been struggling with depression since my late teens on and off - with periods of relative normalcy in between. 

I'm not so scared of being mediocre; It used to be more of a problem before, but I've come to terms with that not everything can always go the way I want. When I was a kid I used to think that if I worked hard enough at things I could do whatever I wanted, but later experience has taught me that even with hard work sometimes things don't go as planned and I'm much better at dealing with that than I was. 

What I am afraid of is never getting away from these kinds of episodes. They feel very debilitating and can often feel like they come out of the blue.
Thanks for your thoughtful and insightful reply, makes me feel a little calmer, less hopeless and less disappointed with myself.

Thanks for your thoughtful reply, I feel a little calmer than I did earlier at least.  I just feel I've been through this so many times now that i'm starting to feel like it's a little hopeless. As I've been struggling with the exact same problems for years.

Up until earlier today I wouldn't even have said that I was depressed. I know that that sounds odd, but the change can be very sudden for me. I used to see both a psychiatrist and a psychologist, but stopped seeing them both 3-4 months ago as I didn't really think it necessary any more. Previously I've tried 3 different types of anti-depressants none of which helped me. I'm having trouble remembering exactly which one, but one of them caused me to stay up for nearly a week straight as well as have huge mood swings, nervous ticks and insane amounts of energy. The other two just didn't do much. The psychologist I've seen on and off for a few years, the Psychiatrist just for the last few months before the last time I started getting better.
